questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UvA have a gender and sexuality department and Mino, which made a lot of courses in this field available, which by far was the most important reason for me for choosing Amsterdam. Furthermore I thought the city was fun and interesting both academically and culturally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved being in Amsterdam and having courses that I chose freely and really go in depth with things that I found so interesting, and meeting people from all over the world was amazing!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - UvAs introduction week and information is extensive and very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails, people to contact and the website with a lot of information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Got it through the university, so very easy, because I just chose it without finding it myself

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are no on-campus living accommodations

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amsterdam has big housing crisis and it can be difficult and expensive to find something to live in. The one I got was, even though cheap, not amazing. I have had a lot of issues and even though I enjoy living here, it has taken some time getting use to the issues.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Applying for up to 45 EC-points and then after seeing how many of the courses you get (randomly allocated) you can pick and choose with the courses you get.  I got all 45 EC points so I could choose which I wanted the most.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: zoom-meeting about course registration - very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just apply for a lot and take it easy - they will help you as much as they can and are just in general very helpful. I ended up needing to change a course the day before it started and they just immediately understood and helped me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mostly had second year courses and then one third year course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more seminars/tutorials and a lot more reading reports and quizzes throughout the weeks, to help students read throughout. Both helpfull but also makes the amount of work a bit bigger.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Gender and Sexuality Studies - 7302A4001Y
Intersectionalities: Race, Gender, and Sexuality - 7332F004BY
Sexual development, parenting and education - 7012KV102Y
“What if…?” An Introduction to Experiments in Sociology - 73330023AY

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Gender and Sexuality Studies  and Intersectionalities: Race, Gender, and Sexuality was absolutely amazing - especially the first one! can highly recommend - both if you've never touched upon gender and sexuality, but also if you have, because its just a different teaching style and themes compared to UCPH

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't attend ones via the university

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums, clubs, parks and winebars

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - very similar to Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dutch people are a bit reserved - mostly have international friends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking culture ;)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- They are all crazy on their bikes and a helmet will be needed but will also make you look like a tourist ;)
- A lot of international students (not only exchange) and they are all very keen on meeting people, so you will meet a lot of interesting people
- The university is so helpful!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the knowledge on gender and sexuality studies

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning - meeting people and trying to socialise as much as possible

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
